body:
Reply with plain text only: no JSON, no code fences, no commentary before or after. Do not send messages to anyone else.

You are drafting dialogue for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon" (an original story; use only the names given here and invent no new people, places, monsters or history). The player leads a party of four adventurers; never name, describe or gender them, and never describe their faces. Setting: Wickermoor Village, in a valley in an autumn that never ends.

SCENE: in the Shade Funeral Home the party speaks to Mori Shade, the village undertaker: slight, ageless, striking white hair, all in black, a grim stately bearing, respected, a well of folklore. She follows the Strangers' faith and learned her trade from Yorgrim the gravedigger. She speaks low, measured and funereal, plainly, with a kind of dry courtesy. Her lines so far, to match in voice and not to repeat: "Step softly, newly arrived. You stand upon ground that has welcomed many before you, and will hold many more before the moon wanes." / "When a companion falls in Druskenvald, the soil does not easily let them go. I wash the brow, fold the hands, and pay the earth its proper due." / "I keep to the Strangers' way: we owe the Ferryman a polite nod and a clean ledger." / "He rowed us all across the dark water once, and he watches still to see if we waste the second breath he gave us." / "Tell me whose memory we are tending, and we shall see them properly laid to rest."

NEW SERVICE: the party can ask Mori to bring back one of their own who has truly died. She works no magic of her own. She goes down to the water in her rites and asks the Ferryman, who keeps the ledger of the dead, to turn his oar back to the near shore; what she asks for is his toll, which she only carries to him. Facts the lines must keep, and no others: (1) the Ferryman will turn his oar only for a soul that went into the water no more than ten days ago; (2) whoever comes back is weak and stumbling for ten days, a shadow of the water clinging to them; (3) the toll is a hundred gold pieces for every rung of craft the fallen one has climbed, so the farther they had come, the more it costs; (4) she keeps no gems and wants no other payment; (5) the party will see the toll set out for each of them before anything is paid, and the offer stands whenever they can pay it; (6) she only does this in the day's hours, from the Twilight Hour to the end of the Evening Hour; the Midnight and Witching hours she gives to the graves. Do not name any number other than "ten days" and "a hundred". Do not use game words (no HP, level, roll, check, save, DC, spell, magic, resurrect, raise dead). Do not promise success or say what the Ferryman is, beyond what is above.

NARRATOR: the Vagrant, an old train conductor telling this tale afterwards in a folksy, warm, wry Southern drawl: word choice and rhythm (reckon, ain't, folks, a spell, a piece), and drop a final g ("tendin'") in about one line in three, not more. Narrator rules: second person ("you"), present tense, one or two sentences, concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a cold), no game words, never tell the player what to feel, never the word "suddenly", no facts the party could not perceive. Do not use {name}. Never mention a fiddle.

FORMAT (exactly this, nothing else): for each node, a row "~ node_id" followed by one row per line: "speaker_id [mood]: Text". The speaker id for Mori is mori_shade. Moods allowed: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary (the mood is optional; Narrator lines take none: "Narrator: Text"). Plain punctuation only: straight quotes, no em dashes, no asterisks, no markdown, no stage directions in brackets, no placeholders. A line is one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Do not write options, menus or any mechanical rows; the game's wiring is added afterwards.

NODES TO WRITE (counts are exact):

~ raising   (the party asks whether one of theirs can be called back; it is within the day's hours)
 - 1 Narrator line: the room's stillness as Mori turns to a black ledger on the desk, a smell or a sound.
 - 4 Mori lines, in this order: she says she does not call anyone back herself, she asks the Ferryman to turn his oar, and the toll is hers only to carry; ten days is the longest he will turn it, and they come back stumbling, with the water still on them, for ten days; the toll is a hundred in gold for each rung of craft the fallen one has climbed, no gems, nothing else; the party will see the sum set out for each of them first, and she asks them to name whom they mean.

~ raising_after   (the party comes back from the sum being set out, whether or not they paid)
 - 1 Mori line: the Ferryman keeps his ledger open and the offer stands as long as the ten days, whenever the purse allows; courteous, no pressure, no mention of whether they paid.

~ raising_closed   (the same question, outside the day's hours)
 - 1 Narrator line: the cold quiet of the room at this hour, the lamps low.
 - 2 Mori lines: she gives this hour to the graves, and the Ferryman takes no asking now; she bids them come back from the Twilight Hour until the Evening Hour is spent, and says the ten days will keep.

~ raising
Narrator: The parlor goes awful still save for the dry rustle of pages as she turns to a black ledger on the desk, smellin' of cedar and cold tallow.
mori_shade [neutral]: I do not call the departed back myself. I only go down to the water, ask the Ferryman to turn his oar, and carry him his toll.
mori_shade [sad]: He turns his oar only for souls in the water no more than ten days. They return weak and stumbling for ten days, the water's shadow clinging on.
mori_shade [neutral]: The toll is a hundred gold pieces for every rung of craft climbed, costing more the farther they came. I keep no gems and ask no other payment.
mori_shade [neutral]: You will see the toll set out for each companion before anything is paid. Tell me whom you mean to call back to the near shore.

~ raising_after
mori_shade [neutral]: The Ferryman keeps his ledger open, and the offer stands for the full ten days, whenever your purse allows.

~ raising_closed
Narrator: The lamps burn low in the parlor, and a damp chill settles deep into the quiet room at this hour.
mori_shade [weary]: The Midnight and Witching hours I give to the graves, and the Ferryman takes no asking now.
mori_shade [neutral]: Come back to me from the Twilight Hour until the Evening Hour is spent. The ten days will keep.
